# Enable IOMMU on the Proxmox host {#sec-iommu}

SSH into the host. See how it boots:

```bash
proxmox-boot-tool status
```

A fresh Proxmox VE 9 install through the UEFI installer entry (@sec-install) uses **systemd-boot** — that's the path below. Edit `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and **append** to the existing line. Do not delete `root=`.

Intel:

```text
intel_iommu=on iommu=pt
```

AMD:

```text
amd_iommu=on iommu=pt
```

Apply:

```bash
proxmox-boot-tool refresh
```

`iommu=pt` is passthrough mode: only devices given to VMs pay IOMMU cost.

::: {.callout-note}
On Proxmox kernels 6.8+, Intel often turns IOMMU on without `intel_iommu=on`. Keep the flag anyway so the intent is obvious in `/proc/cmdline`.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## If `proxmox-boot-tool status` reports GRUB instead

Unusual for a fresh UEFI install, but possible if the installer picked a BIOS/legacy target or CSM wasn't fully disabled (@sec-bios). Edit `/etc/default/grub` instead:

```bash
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet intel_iommu=on iommu=pt"    # Intel
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="quiet amd_iommu=on iommu=pt"      # AMD
```

Apply with `update-grub`. Otherwise, re-check the BIOS boot-mode settings and reinstall in UEFI mode — the rest of this book assumes systemd-boot.
:::

## Load VFIO at boot

Add to `/etc/modules`:

```text
vfio
vfio_iommu_type1
vfio_pci
```

`vfio_virqfd` was folded into other modules on newer kernels. Skip it if `modprobe` complains.

Reboot, then check:

```bash
dmesg | grep -e DMAR -e IOMMU -e AMD-Vi
cat /proc/cmdline
```

You want DMAR or AMD-Vi tables found, "IOMMU enabled", and the flags in the command line.
